area: Input buffering vs the OG's measured semantics (busy-state gating, deferred strokes, after-attack window)

item_verdicts.title: Generic fixed-window input buffer (5–15 frames / 80–250 ms) as the stroke mechanism
item_verdicts.why: Sources check out: salivity says verbatim "Developers usually set this between 5 to 15 frames (roughly 80 to 250 milliseconds)" AND "If the window expires before the character is free, the input is discarded"; SmashWiki gives Brawl 10 frames and Ultimate "the buffer window is now 9 frames, down from 10" (=the cited 9–10); Dustloop/GBVSR gives "the input buffer ... is extended to 6 frames, for a total window of 7 frames" after wake-up/air recovery. Repo check passes exactly as claimed: src/core/Sim.ts applyStroke consults phase, autoSlash and point-count only — playerBusyUntilFrame is WRITTEN there (swing.windup+active+recovery) and READ only in the auto-slash decision path, so a manual stroke executes immediately; `grep -rn BUFFER src/config/` returns nothing, so the "do not add a *_BUFFER_MS constant" guidance targets a real absence. Two attacks land, neither fatal: (a) "SFV 3" is supported by NONE of the three cited sources — salivity names no game at all; (b) the ~1.4 s PENDING row is single-instance and was NOT among the three claims re-derived in the §S24-H verify re-run (commit a35af8d, 2026-08-12), so the REJECT verdict rests securely on K1 alone — which that pass DID confirm ("K1-rejection CONFIRMED (one tick, no flash, no HP change, no dash)").
item_verdicts.correction: Delete the "SFV 3" datum — it is unsupported by any of the three cited sources (salivity names no specific game; SmashWiki and Dustloop cover Smash and GBVSR only). Cite the canon band as "salivity 5–15 frames / 80–250 ms; Smash Brawl 10 → Ultimate 9; GBVSR 6-frame extension = 7-frame total window on wake-up". Also weaken the second leg: the ~1.4 s deferral rests on ONE unverified instance (Honda f0116–f0138) that the 2026-08-12 §S24-H verify re-run did not re-derive; the REJECT adjudication stands on the CONFIRMED K1 row alone.

item_verdicts.title: OG-faithful spec: busy-state gating + single-slot deferred-stroke queue in Sim, blink rendered by the scene
item_verdicts.why: Every named seam exists as described: Sim.ts carries `private playerBusyUntilFrame = ZERO` with the comment "auto-slash never decides mid-swing (D7). Stun is NOT modelled in this Sim (flagged)."; applyStroke(stroke, source: StrokeSource = 'manual') is the single entry point and the auto path calls `this.applyStroke(new DrawnStroke(points), 'auto')`; dealDamage is the single damage funnel (enemy strike, chi punch, projectile all route through it); SimEvent is an established discriminated union that already carries a scene-drawn-stroke precedent (`autoStroke`); `get frame()` is public; DuelScene.finishStroke calls sim.applyStroke synchronously. §S24-F does supply knockdown ~6 ticks and "global hit-stop ... 3 content ticks (~200 ms)". BUT two parameterization errors survive scrutiny. (1) SEED CONFLATION: §S24-E's "mid-combo hit = 4–5 ticks recovery" sits under "Landing holds (for the partb loop)" alongside "chained strike = 0–1 tick" and "kill/final = pose holds until input/cinematic" — these are the STRIKER's post-contact animation holds, not the victim's hit-stun, so seeding a victim-side hitRecoveryUntilFrame from them mixes two different actors' clocks. (2) ARITHMETIC: SLASH_FRAMES in src/config/timing.ts totals 12 (light 4/4/4), 16 (balanced 4/4/8), 20 (heavy 4/4/12) sim frames = 0.20–0.33 s, so a DEFER gate keyed on playerBusyUntilFrame can release at most ~0.33 s later — roughly 4× short of the measured ~1.4 s hang. §S24-A.2 says the real release condition is arrival ("Hang duration is not fixed: 2–22 ticks observed — execution waits for the fighter to arrive"), not swing-recovery end. (3) LABELLING: PENDING_BLINK_OFF cannot be CONTRACT — §S24-A.6 records it as "3-on/1–2-off at the sampling floor" and §S24 states all timings carry the ±1 content-tick floor, which is exactly the width of the 1-vs-2 ambiguity.
item_verdicts.correction: Three fixes to the spec. (a) Seed hitRecoveryUntilFrame from §S24-F (victim-side: global hit-stop 3 ticks; knockdown stands up by ~6 ticks; knock-up lands 7 ticks), NOT from §S24-E's 4–5-tick figure — that is the STRIKER's landing hold (§S24-E "Landing holds", same list as "chained strike = 0–1 tick" and "kill/final pose holds"), and belongs to the DEFER window instead. (b) The DEFER release cannot be `frameCount >= playerBusyUntilFrame`: SLASH_FRAMES totals only 12/16/20 sim frames (0.20–0.33 s) against the measured ~1.4 s pending hang, and §S24-A.2 gives the actual gate — the stroke hangs 2–22 ticks because "execution waits for the fighter to arrive". Release on arrival-or-recovery, whichever is later, and record the mismatch as an open A12.2 question. (c) Tag PENDING_BLINK_ON/OFF INFERRED, not CONTRACT — §S24-A.6's "1–2-off at the sampling floor" is unresolvable at the ±1-content-tick floor and was not re-derived by the 2026-08-12 verify pass.

item_verdicts.title: Song's 'After Attack Delay' (Game Developer, 2005) — the canon rationale for DEFER-not-drop during own-swing recovery
item_verdicts.why: The source is real and says precisely what is attributed to it: gamedeveloper.com/audio/improving-the-combat-impact-of-action-games, Jiesang Song, main game programmer of Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders — "In many games including Devil May Cry, POP:WW, and Ninja Gaiden, after an attack motion, the character animation lingers before ending so the player can continue the next attack even after missing the button press timing." The repo cross-link checks out too: that exact quote is already excerpted in docs/research/2026-08-05-improvements-research.md (Song URL at ~line 129, the After-Attack-Delay quote at ~line 573; ~line 364 is a different Song quote about blade trails). §S24-E's "chained strike = 0–1 tick (dojo S1)" exists verbatim and is attacker-side, so it is the right row for a chain claim. The one defect is the parameterization sentence: "acceptance window = the whole playerBusyUntilFrame period (§S24-A.6 PENDING shows ~1.4 s)" equates two quantities that differ by ~4× in this repo — playerBusyUntilFrame maxes at 20 sim frames (0.33 s) from SLASH_FRAMES heavy 4/4/12.
item_verdicts.correction: Strike the equation "acceptance window = the whole playerBusyUntilFrame period (~1.4 s)". In this repo playerBusyUntilFrame is SLASH_FRAMES-derived and lasts 12/16/20 sim frames (0.20/0.27/0.33 s); the measured ~1.4 s hang is §S24-A.2's wait-for-arrival, a different clock. State it as: acceptance lasts until the fighter is actionable AND has arrived (§S24-A.2, 2–22 ticks), of which the swing-recovery window is only the first 0.2–0.33 s.

item_verdicts.title: Reject/defer boundary, pending-slot replacement policy, and deferral timeout are underdetermined — measure before pinning CONTRACT
item_verdicts.why: The MEASURE_FIRST core is right and is in fact strengthened by the ledger state the research could not see. Canon citations verify: SmashWiki Brawl "Any action out of tumble hitstun" cannot be buffered ✓; Smash 4 "a built-in hierarchy now dictates in what order actions are used" ✓; Dustloop GBVSR 6-frame extension / 7-frame total on wake-up ✓; Yosi Spring supports both cited points (newer-input priority is offered as the fix for unwanted buffered actions, and buffered inputs must be "cleared" so they cannot re-trigger). But two ledger statements in the item are stale: the K1 anchor and the pending-verdict status. §S24-H (committed a35af8d, "SESSION24 A12.1 verify LANDED") now reads: "K1-rejection CONFIRMED ... with an anchor fix: K1 starts ~30–60 px AHEAD of the body centre, not 29 px behind; only the K2-further-ahead contrast (+50 px) survives", and the same block appears in the binding "Verify-pass corrections (2026-08-12) — these WIN" list (item 3). Per the verifier brief this is a post-research ledger change, so it corrects rather than convicts the item — and it does not rescue the confound: position and timing are still jointly varying, just by ~50 px instead of 69.
item_verdicts.correction: Update the K1 datum to the §S24-H verify-pass correction (which WINS over §S24-A.6): K1 starts ~30–60 px AHEAD of the body centre, not 29 px behind, and the surviving K1-vs-K2 placement contrast is ~+50 px, not 69 px — the position/timing confound stands at "2 ticks AND ~50 px". Also drop "§S24-H's adversarial verify pass is still [VERDICT PENDING]": the re-run (wf_56ff205f-341, 3 skeptics) landed 2026-08-12 with three WEAKENED-with-corrections verdicts. It reinforces the item's premise — the PENDING/blink row was NOT among the claims re-derived, so it remains the thinnest evidence in the area.

item_verdicts.title: Residual use of generic-canon numbers: INFERRED seeds and latency sanity bands only
item_verdicts.why: Every checkable assertion holds. Repo: Sim.queueSkill is exactly as described — "Edge-triggered skill press (hotbar 1/2/3) — consumed on the next tick. Discarded outside 'fighting', like strokes" with `if (this.phaseState !== 'fighting') return; this.queuedSkill = verb;` — so no canon skill-buffer work is needed. src/config/CLAUDE.md does mandate the CONTRACT/INFERRED/Spec-fixed label on every value, so the INFERRED-tag requirement is correctly stated. Sources: salivity's 80–250 ms band verified verbatim; §00/§S24 give the 66.7 ms content-tick floor; Dustloop's GBVSR 6/7-frame wake-up extension verified as the right INFERRED seed shape; Yosi Spring explicitly gives the consumed-input clearing pattern ("allowing the input buffer to be 'cleared' ... so then it can't possibly trigger anything else"). Two honest nits that do not damage the item: the Thorson thread confirms "If you press and hold the jump button a short time before landing, you will jump on the exact frame that you land" but states NO frame count, so "few-frame" is the research's own gloss, not the source's; and the proposed latency test is already true today (DuelScene.finishStroke calls sim.applyStroke synchronously inside the pointerup handler), making it a regression guard rather than a new bound — which is what the item claims it is ("a test, not a constant").

overall_note: Attack summary: 5 of the cited URLs were fetched live and all 5 support the claims attributed to them (SmashWiki Buffer, gamedeveloper.com Song 2005, salivity, threadreaderapp Thorson, Yosi Spring). No fabricated or dead source. The Dustloop GBVSR URL returns HTTP 403 to WebFetch but is a live indexed page whose content — \"the input buffer ... is extended to 6 frames, for a total window of 7 frames\" after wake-up/air recovery — matches the citation, so it is NOT a dead-link kill. Repo re-check: every ALREADY_DONE/REJECT-supporting repo fact is real — applyStroke ignores playerBusyUntilFrame for manual strokes (it only writes it; the sole read is the auto-slash guard), \"Stun is NOT modelled in this Sim (flagged)\", queueSkill's 1-frame edge trigger, the SimEvent union with its `autoStroke` precedent, dealDamage as the single damage funnel, public `get frame()`, and zero *_BUFFER constants in src/config/. Ledger re-check: §S24-A.6, §S24-C's build-consequence sentence, §S24-E's landing holds, §S24-F's 3-tick hit-stop and ~6-tick knockdown all say what is claimed; §00b overturns nothing in this area. Nothing was REFUTED — the area's central adjudication (reject a generic fixed-window buffer; build state-conditional reject/defer) survives intact. Three defects worth the parent agent's attention before A12.2 is specced: (1) the 4–5-tick hit-recovery seed is taken from §S24-E's STRIKER-side landing holds and must come from §S24-F's victim-side rows instead; (2) SLASH_FRAMES totals only 12/16/20 sim frames (0.20–0.33 s), so a DEFER gate keyed on playerBusyUntilFrame cannot reproduce the measured ~1.4 s hang — §S24-A.2's wait-for-arrival (2–22 ticks) is the real release condition; (3) the K1 anchor moved in the 2026-08-12 verify block (now ~30–60 px AHEAD of centre, contrast ~+50 px), and the PENDING/blink row was never re-derived, so nothing about the blink may be tagged CONTRACT.
